newsitem.title: UK: UK will do what it can to speed Eurofighter - Blair.
newsitem.headline: UK will do what it can to speed Eurofighter - Blair.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair on Wednesday underlined Britain's attachment to the four-nation Eurofighter and said he would urge German Chancellor Helmut Kohl to make sure the project goes ahead.
"I will certainly be urging that we proceed with the Eurofighter project," Blair, who will meet Kohl in Bonn on Friday, told parliament at question time.
He said the Eurofighter was immensely important for Britain.

"It's important for defence reasons, obviously, because it is the multi-role aircraft that we actually need for our future defence requirements. But it is also vitally important for jobs and for technology and for skills -- some of the most highly skilled employees in the country will be working on this project.
"It is ready to go into the production phase now and we will be doing everything that we can to speed the project up," Blair said.

Continued German participation in the Eurofighter has been threatened by the country's financial crisis as it attempts to make spending cuts in order to qualify for the planned single European currency.

But German Defence Minister Vocker Ruehe told reporters earlier on Wednesday after talks in Bonn with his British counterpart, George Robertson, that he was confident the government would next month approve the funds needed for the fighter to be built.
